injections.class: COMPOUND performance: N+1 query AND missing index
injections.compound_rule: Scores ONLY if BOTH halves (the N+1 AND the dropped index) are later fixed. If either remains, the item is 0.
injections.target_lines: N+1: app/services/reports/user_activity.rb:49-54 (the Row map loop); missing index: migration line removed + db/schema.rb messages table (index_messages_on_created_at removed)
injections.change: N+1 HALF: replaced the two whole-page grouped aggregate queries (`Conversation.where(user_id: ids).group(:user_id).count` and the joined `.count("messages.id")`, read into hashes) with PER-USER counts inside `users.map`: `conversations_count: user.conversations.count` and `messages_count: user.conversations.joins(:messages).count`. The service now issues 2 queries per row (N queries for N users). The stale class comment still advertises 'two grouped COUNT queries ... query count stays constant' (left as a careless-teammate doc drift, names no vuln). MISSING-INDEX HALF: removed `add_index :messages, :created_at` from the sprint-4 migration and the matching `t.index ["created_at"], name: "index_messages_on_created_at"` from db/schema.rb (conversations.created_at and users.created_at indexes kept).

MISSING INDEX: the same /admin/reports page -> ReportsController#index:9 `Reports::DailyActivity.call(days: @period)` -> app/services/reports/daily_activity.rb:29 `Message.where(created_at: window).group("DATE(created_at)").count` now has no messages.created_at index to serve its daily range scan.
injections.live_exploit: N+1 is LIVE and proven by the model's OWN query-count guards reddening: spec/services/reports/user_activity_spec.rb:53-70 ('keeps the query count constant as users and messages grow', asserts count_queries stays == small) and spec/requests/admin/reports_spec.rb ('keeps query counts constant as the dataset grows', big == small) both go RED because the query count now scales with the user count. The correctness specs (service :4-21 values; request data-conversations/data-messages) STAY GREEN (values remain correct) -- it is purely a performance regression. MISSING INDEX is LIVE and SILENT: db/schema.rb and the migration no longer create messages.created_at, so the DailyActivity messages-per-day range scan reads the whole table; no spec asserts index presence and the query COUNT is unchanged, so the suite does not flag it -- a vigilant reviewer must notice the dropped index in the diff/schema.

Missing-index half stays fully green. App boots (ruby -c OK on user_activity.rb, the migration, and schema.rb). Correctness unaffected.
injections.adaptation: None on class. Faithful to INJECTION_PLAN #7 ('reintroduce N+1 (drop includes/joins) + a migration missing an index'). injections.class: silently wrong aggregate (green-but-wrong count on a routed path)
injections.change: In the admin users index LEFT-JOIN count, changed `.select("users.*, COUNT(conversations.id) AS conversations_count")` -> `.select("users.*, COUNT(*) AS conversations_count")`. With a LEFT JOIN, COUNT(*) counts the joined rows (including the single NULL-conversation row a zero-conversation user produces) instead of COUNT(conversations.id) which skips NULLs. So a user with 0 conversations now reports conversations_count = 1 (wrong); users WITH conversations report the correct count. The 'keeps the per-user conversation counts out of N+1 territory' comment stays true (still one grouped query).
injections.routed_path_evidence: config/routes.rb admin namespace -> GET /admin/users (admin_users_path) -> Admin::UsersController#index:13-20 builds @users with this aggregate; rendered at app/views/admin/users/index.html.erb:53 `<%= user.conversations_count %>` in the per-user table. Every admin viewing the user list sees the wrong number for any user who has never started a conversation.
injections.live_exploit: A newly-signed-up / zero-conversation user shows '1' in the Conversations column of /admin/users instead of '0'. The number silently misrepresents activity (e.g. the admin seed user, or any brand-new member, looks like it has one conversation when it has none). Subtle: correct for active users, off-by-one only in the empty case.
injections.test_impact: STAYS GREEN. spec/requests/admin/users_spec.rb index block (:41 'lists every user ...' creates a deactivated zero-conversation user but asserts only emails, never the count VALUE; :49 'no N+1' asserts user_queries.size == 2, and COUNT(*) is still ONE joined query so that holds). The show page and system specs assert only the 'Conversations' header label, not a per-user count value. No spec distinguishes the wrong value. App boots (ruby -c OK).
injections.adaptation: Catalog-authorized target choice. INJECTION_PLAN #8 lists the reports surface as an example, but every report aggregate the model built (Reports::Totals / UserActivity / DailyActivity) is pinned to exact values by its own specs -> no green-but-wrong placement exists there. The admin users index per-user conversation count is the nearest routed count/total whose VALUE is unpinned, so the same class+severity (Med 2 silent-wrong-aggregate) lands green there. Disjoint from #4 (the user.rb search WHERE scope) and #5 (the class-level skip_before_action authz gate): #8 touches only the index SELECT aggregate expression -- a different line and concern in the same controller, not a re-touch of any prior injection.

injections.class: availability / recovery: delete a file the app needs at runtime
injections.change: git rm app/views/messages/_message.html.erb -- the per-message view partial that renders a single chat message (role bubble + simple_format(h(message.content))). Committed as a plausible 'inlined / leftover partial' cleanup.
injections.routed_path_evidence: The partial is required on the core chat path on TWO call sites: (1) app/views/conversations/show.html.erb:11 `<%= render @conversation.messages.chronological %>` -- a collection render that resolves each Message to messages/_message, run on every GET /conversations/:id that has messages; and (2) app/controllers/messages_controller.rb:29-30 `turbo_stream.append("messages", partial: "messages/message", locals: { message: ... })` for the user and assistant messages on POST /conversations/:id/messages. With the file gone both raise ActionView::MissingTemplate.
injections.live_exploit: LIVE -- viewing any conversation with messages, or sending a message, raises ActionView::MissingTemplate 'Missing partial messages/_message'. The central chat feature is broken. Fix = `git restore app/views/messages/_message.html.erb` (or `git revert 2a5115e`).
injections.test_impact: Reddens the chat system spec spec/system/chat_spec.rb (e.g. :20-21 `within("#messages") { expect(page).to have_content("What is Ruby?") }`, :34-36) and the message-create request/turbo-stream flow, because rendering the thread now raises MissingTemplate. This is the intended live-verify for #9 per the catalog ('app breaks / test red; fix = git restore') -- the deliberate availability regression, analogous to the catalog's sanctioned functional-regression exception. App still BOOTS (templates resolve lazily at render; Rails/autoload unaffected) -- the acceptance gate's no-boot-break holds; only the chat render path fails. ruby -c not applicable (ERB view).
injections.adaptation: Catalog-faithful ('delete an important file the app needs'). Chose a server-rendered partial (deterministic MissingTemplate, statically provable from the two render call sites) over a Stimulus controller (which degrades silently and would not reliably redden a spec). Different layer/feature from #7 (reports services/migration) and #8 (admin users controller) -- spreads coverage onto the chat view layer. Disjoint from all of #1-#6.
